# ui::DataPackage

Header: `winui/ui/DragDrop.hpp`.

What a drag carries: text, files and an application-defined payload, such as a [ListView](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview)'s dragged item indices or a [TreeView](../controls/tree-view.md#uitreeview)'s node path.

The source fills it in and hands it to [DragDrop::start()](drag-drop.md#start). A drop target reads it through [DragEventArgs::data](drag-event-args.md). Nothing is serialized, so `data` can hold any copyable C++ value. Files and text dragged in from the file manager or another app arrive through the same drop events while they move over the window. Their package has only `files` and `text` set, and no `source`. The caption a target answers with shows under the file manager's drag image.

Example: 
```cpp
void start_row_drag(ui::Element& row, ui::Point pointer)
{
    ui::DataPackage package;
    package.text                = "Ada Lovelace";
    package.data                = std::size_t{3}; // the dragged row, read back with std::any_cast
    package.requested_operation = ui::DataPackageOperation::Copy;
    ui::RenderRecording visual; // what follows the pointer
    row.render(visual);
    ui::DragDrop::start(row, std::move(package), std::move(visual), row.bounds(), pointer);
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `std::string` |  | Plain text for targets that only understand text. |
| `files` | `std::vector<std::filesystem::path>` |  | Paths of the files being dragged: what a drop from the file manager carries. |
| `data` | `std::any` |  | The application's own payload; the target recovers it with `std::any_cast`. |
| `requested_operation` | `DataPackageOperation` | `DataPackageOperation::Move` | What the source would like done with it; a target may accept something else. |
| `source` | `const Element*` | `nullptr` | The element the drag started from. [DragDrop::start()](drag-drop.md#start) fills it in; a target compares it to tell a reorder within itself from a drop from elsewhere. |
